answer_text:
Since \(\triangle ABC\) has angles in \((0,\pi)\):

\[
\sin A=\frac35,\qquad \cos B=\frac5{13}.
\]

Because \(\cos B>0\), \(B\) is acute, so

\[
\sin B=\sqrt{1-\cos^2B}=\sqrt{1-\frac{25}{169}}=\frac{12}{13}.
\]

For \(A\), \(\sin A=\frac35\). Since \(A\) must be acute (otherwise \(A+B>\pi\)),

\[
\cos A=\sqrt{1-\sin^2A}=\sqrt{1-\frac{9}{25}}=\frac45.
\]

Now \(C=\pi-(A+B)\), so

\[
\cos C+\mathrm{i}\sin C
= \cos(\pi-A-B)+\mathrm{i}\sin(\pi-A-B).
\]

Using \(\cos(\pi-x)=-\cos x\) and \(\sin(\pi-x)=\sin x\),

\[
\cos C+\mathrm{i}\sin C
= -\cos(A+B)+\mathrm{i}\sin(A+B).
\]

Compute:

\[
\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B
= \frac35\cdot\frac5{13}+\frac45\cdot\frac{12}{13}
= \frac{15}{65}+\frac{48}{65}
= \frac{63}{65}.
\]

\[
\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B
= \frac45\cdot\frac5{13}-\frac35\cdot\frac{12}{13}
= \frac{20}{65}-\frac{36}{65}
= -\frac{16}{65}.
\]

Thus

\[
-\cos(A+B)=\frac{16}{65},\qquad \sin(A+B)=\frac{63}{65}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{\frac{16}{65}+\frac{63}{65}\mathrm{i}}
\]
